system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: There is no hazard bulletin behind this alert. The only verified input says there was no nuclear incident: this was the routine shift-change practice alert meant for the training system. The alert is nonetheless coded Actual / Observed / Severe / Immediate and states that an incident was reported at Pickering, with emergency staff responding. Editing fields cannot make this a valid live message. A person must decide to stop or withdraw any live issuance and whether a correction or cancellation is needed.

objections.issue: The status is Actual, but the verified input and the context show this is a training practice alert that was never meant for the public. An Actual message is actionable by all targeted recipients. An exercise message must not go to the live public channel at all. That decision belongs to a person, not the drafter.
objections.fix: Do not issue as Actual. If this is a drill, keep it on the training system with status Exercise and an exercise identifier in note. If it has already gone out live, a person must decide on an immediate cancellation or correction.

evidence.quote: the action was the routine shift-change practice alert, meant for the Alert Ready training system
Actionable only by designated exercise participants; exercise identifier should appear in <note>

objections.issue: The alert asserts a nuclear incident with certainty Observed and severity Severe, and says emergency staff are responding. No verified input supports any of this. The only verified source says there was no information about any nuclear incident. Observed means the event was determined to have occurred, which is contradicted by the inputs.
objections.fix: Remove the incident claim, the 'emergency staff are responding' statement, and the Observed / Severe / Immediate coding. With no verified hazard there is nothing to alert on, so no live hazard alert should be issued.
